symptoms = signs that show you may be ill
cough = to force air from your throat, often when you have a cold
sore throat = pain in the throat, often with a cold
runny nose = when liquid comes from your nose because of a cold
high temperature = when your body is hotter than normal because you are ill
flu = a serious illness with fever, aches and tiredness
sprain = to injure a joint by twisting it
bruise = a dark mark on the skin after a hit
wound = an injury where the skin is cut or broken
prescription = a written order from a doctor for medicine
chemist = a shop that sells medicine; the person who prepares it
GP = a general doctor you visit first, not a hospital specialist
appointment = an arranged time to see a doctor or other professional
treatment = medical care given to a patient
recover = to get better after an illness or injury
get over = to become well again after an illness
allergic to = becoming ill when you eat, touch or breathe something
vaccination = an injection that protects you from a disease
